name: RT-2 (Vision-Language-Action Models, Brohan et al., 2023)
observations: Source: arXiv:2307.15818v1 (28 Jul 2023), Google DeepMind, 26 pages. Local copy: pdf/embodied_ai_papers/RT-2, Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control, Anthony Brohan et al., 2023, v1_compressed.pdf

Thesis: a single end-to-end model can both map robot observations to actions and inherit Internet-scale vision+language knowledge, by co-fine-tuning a pretrained VLM on robot trajectories AND the original web VQA/captioning data.

Core trick (Sec 3.2): express actions as text tokens. 6-DoF end-effector delta position and rotation (dx, dy, dz, drx, dry, drz), gripper extension, and a terminate command = 8 integers. All continuous dims are discretized into 256 uniform bins; the action is serialized as a space-separated string, e.g. 1 128 91 241 5 101 127.

Tokenizer mapping differs per backbone: PaLI-X has unique tokens for integers up to 1000 so bins map directly; PaLM-E overwrites the 256 least-frequently-used tokens as the action vocabulary (a form of symbol tuning). No new action-specific layers or parameters are added; weights are fully shared between language and action tasks.

Training data format: VQA-style prompt, question asks what action the robot should take for the instruction, answer is the action token string, paired with the camera image. Web data is mixed into the same batch with the robot dataset upsampled to keep a usable robot/web ratio.

Co-fine-tuning is the key ablation win (Sec 4.3): training from scratch performs very poorly even at 5B; robot-only fine-tuning forgets VLM concepts; co-fine-tuning generalizes best. Larger model size also helps (5B vs 55B).
Output constraint: during decoding, sample only over valid action tokens when prompted with a robot-action task, while leaving the full natural-language vocabulary available for ordinary VQA tasks.

Real-time inference (Sec 3.3): models up to 55B params are far too big for on-robot GPUs, so they are deployed in a multi-TPU cloud service queried over the network. Throughput: 55B gives 1-3 Hz, 5B gives about 5 Hz.

Instantiations: RT-2-PaLI-X (5B and 55B, from PaLI-X) and RT-2-PaLM-E (12B, from PaLM-E). Robot data inherited from RT-1: 13 robots, 17 months, office kitchen, 200+ seen tasks, each trajectory language-annotated with a verb plus nouns.

Results: about 6000 real evaluation trajectories. Seen-task performance is similar to RT-1 (35M params); on generalization to unseen objects/backgrounds/environments RT-2 is roughly 2x better than RT-1 and MOO and roughly 6x better than the VC-1/R3M baselines. On emergent skills (symbol understanding, reasoning, human recognition) it exceeds 3x the average success of the best baseline. Language-Table sim with 3B PaLI: 90 +/- 10 vs LAVA 77 +/- 4, RT-1 74, BC-Zero 72.

Chain-of-thought variant (Sec 4.4): insert a natural-language Plan step before the action tokens, e.g. Instruction: I am hungry. Plan: pick rxbar chocolate. Action: 1 128 124 136 121 158 111 255. Only a few hundred gradient steps of tuning; enables multi-stage semantic reasoning such as picking a rock as an improvised hammer or choosing an energy drink for someone who is tired.

Limitations (Sec 5): web pretraining transfers semantics and visual concepts but NOT new motor skills; the physical repertoire stays bounded by the robot data distribution. Compute cost is high, so real-time inference is the bottleneck for high-frequency control; the paper suggests quantization and distillation. It also flags scarcity of openly fine-tunable VLMs, pointing to LLaVA as a hoped-for direction.

Explicitly contrasts with prior VLM-in-robotics work (CLIPort, MOO, say-can style planners): no restricted 2D action space, no calibrated camera requirement, and no separate high-level planner; the VLM itself is the low-level closed-loop policy.

name: VLA (Vision-Language-Action) Recipe
observations: Reusable recipe distilled from RT-2: (1) start from a pretrained VLM; (2) discretize the robot action vector into bins and serialize it as text; (3) build VQA-format image+instruction to action-token-string training examples; (4) co-fine-tune on robot data mixed with the original web VLM data, upsampling robot data; (5) constrain decoding to the action token set at inference; (6) close the loop by de-tokenizing tokens back to continuous actions at each control step.

Design invariants that matter: keep language and action heads shared with no action-only parameters, preserve the pretraining data mixture to avoid catastrophic forgetting, and keep the model large because capability scales with the VLM backbone size.

Practical inference requirement: this class of model needs a serving layer (remote or batched inference) unless quantized or distilled, because 1-5 Hz is the control-rate ceiling for multi-billion-parameter backbones.
Distinct from modular LLM-planner plus low-level-controller stacks: semantic knowledge reaches low-level action prediction directly rather than crossing a state-machine boundary.

name: LeRobot (Hugging Face)
observations: Library ID /huggingface/lerobot, v0.6.1, High source reputation, about 4500 code snippets. End-to-end robot learning stack: dataset format, teleop recording, training, and evaluation.

Ships vision-language-action policies out of the box via policy type smolvla, with load_vlm_weights to initialize from the VLM backbone. This is the closest open equivalent of the RT-2 idea in a maintained library. It also offers ACT and diffusion policies for pure imitation learning.

Training entrypoint: lerobot-train with arguments --policy.type=smolvla, --policy.load_vlm_weights=true, --policy.repo_id, --dataset.repo_id, --dataset.video_backend=torchcodec, --steps=100000, --batch_size=64, --output_dir.

Evaluation is a separate entrypoint: lerobot-eval with --policy.path, --env.type (libero, isaaclab_arena, vlabench, libero_plus), --env.task, --eval.batch_size, --eval.n_episodes, --policy.device=cuda.

Data side: LeRobotDataset.create(repo_id, fps, features, robot_type, use_videos=True) plus record_loop(...) for teleop episodes, then dataset.save_episode(), dataset.finalize(), dataset.push_to_hub(). CLI equivalent is lerobot-record with --dataset.num_episodes and --dataset.single_task. The single_task instruction string is where RT-2-style language annotation enters.

Camera key plumbing matters in practice: --rename_map and --env.camera_name_mapping translate between environment camera names (agentview_image, wrist_image) and dataset keys (observation.images.camera1).
Why it maps to RT-2: it supplies the robot dataset plus instruction annotation plus VLM-backbone policy pieces in an open, reproducible form rather than as a cloud-served 55B model.

name: Hugging Face Transformers (PaliGemma VLM fine-tuning)
observations: Library ID /huggingface/transformers, versions v4.46 through v5.x, High reputation. Supplies the pretrained VLM backbone the RT-2 recipe needs, and is the same model lineage as RT-2's PaLI-X.
PaliGemma is the practical open stand-in for PaLI-X / PaLM-E: AutoProcessor.from_pretrained with google/paligemma-3b-pt-224, then processor(text=prompt, images=image, return_tensors=pt).

Key API for the action-as-text recipe: the processor suffix argument builds the target labels, i.e. processor(images=image, text=prompt, suffix=action_string). This is directly equivalent to RT-2's question plus answer action-token construction.

Fine-tuning loop: Trainer(model=..., args=..., train_dataset=..., processing_class=processor, data_collator=...) then trainer.push_to_hub(). Use DataCollatorForLanguageModeling(mlm=False) for plain causal-LM targets.

Gap to be aware of: Transformers gives VLM training but not robot control loops, dataset formats, or action de-tokenization. Those belong to LeRobot. The two libraries are complementary layers of the same VLA stack.
Caveat carried over from RT-2 Sec 5: inspect the model tokenizer before reserving action bins. Models with unique integer tokens map bins directly; others require overwriting rare tokens.
